purpose: Probe: does cross-frame conditioning reduce the teacher's temporal instability, which KB Decision 57 identified as M6's root cause?
not_a_regeneration: This generates one short span, not the 990-frame target set. It answers whether a regeneration would pay before it is spent.
metric: mask-weighted mean |I_t - W(I_{t-1}, V_t)| — the M6 gate's quantity
change_under_test: init_t = M_t * W(styled_{t-1}, V_t) + (1 - M_t) * native_t, instead of init_t = native_t. Seed, prompt, strength, guidance and controlnet scale are unchanged.
caveats: Cross-frame conditioning makes generation SEQUENTIAL (no parallelism) and can accumulate drift over a long span; this probe covers a short one. It also changes what the alignment gates see, so KB Decision 32's four gates would have to be re-run on any regenerated set.
verdict: REFUTED — cross-frame conditioning as tested makes the teacher 11x LESS temporally stable
mechanism_hypothesis: Consistent with compounding re-stylisation, not with flicker. At strength 0.50 the pipeline re-denoises half the trajectory; feeding it an ALREADY-STYLED frame applies the style a second time, then a third, and so on down the chain. Each frame is a bigger departure from the last, so the frame-to-frame difference grows rather than shrinks. The engine's own motion is not the problem — native_engine is unchanged at ~0.00016 across both runs. NOT CONFIRMED: the per-frame images were not retained, so this is the reading most consistent with 378x, not a measurement.
what_this_rules_out: Naive appearance propagation through img2img. It does NOT rule out cross-frame conditioning in general — latent-space blending, a lower strength on chained frames, or true cross-frame attention are untested and would each need their own probe. No further variant is proposed here.
cost_avoided: Regenerating 990 targets, re-running KB Decision 32's four alignment gates, and retraining Models A, C and D — roughly a day of compute — on a change that would have made the root cause worse.
